draft.title: Types of investigations
card: Controlled experiment

the researcher changes one variable (the independent variable) and measures its effect on another (the dependent variable), while controlling other variables. It is suited to questions about cause and effect.
Correlational study
measures two variables as they are, without changing either, to see if they are related. It shows a relationship but cannot show that one variable causes the other.
Case study
examines one person, group or event in depth. It suits rare or unusual cases that cannot be set up in an experiment.
Others
Fieldwork collects data in a real-world setting. A literature review compares findings from many existing studies. A simulation models a real situation or process in a safe, artificial setting.
draft.remember: Match the investigation to the question: cause and effect needs a controlled experiment, and a relationship needs a correlational study.

a.q: A researcher wants to know if a new sleep routine causes better exam scores. Which investigation is best suited?
opts: A controlled experiment
A correlational study
A literature review
A case study
a.why: Only a controlled experiment changes one variable and controls the others, so it can show cause and effect. A correlational study is tempting, but it only shows that two variables are related, not that one causes the other.
a.clue: Which type changes one variable and controls the rest?

b.q: Dr Lee surveys 300 Year 12 students in Geelong on their weekly screen time and their sleep hours. She changes nothing. She finds that more screen time goes with less sleep. What can she conclude?
opts: The two are related, but screen time may not cause it
Screen time causes students to sleep less
Less sleep causes students to use screens more
The two variables are not related to each other
b.why: She measured both variables without changing either, so this is a correlational study. It can show a relationship but not which variable causes the other. The second option is tempting, but only a controlled experiment could support a cause claim.
b.clue: Did she change any variable, or only measure them?

b.best: The two are related, but screen time may not cause it

problems.detail: The remember line says cause and effect 'needs' a controlled experiment and a relationship 'needs' a correlational study. The card only says each is 'suited to' its question, and controlled experiments can also show relationships, so the line sorts the types more rigidly than the card does.

The right option is clearly the longest and the only hedged one ('but screen time may not cause it'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea. Its 'it' is also vague; it should name 'less sleep'.
Why (a) says 'Only a controlled experiment...', while the card says a controlled experiment 'is suited to' cause-and-effect questions.
Why (b) says 'only a controlled experiment could support a cause claim', which is absolute wording where the card says 'suited to'.

check.summary: Facts and intended answers are correct. The remember line is more absolute than the card ('needs' rather than 'suited to'), the right option in (b) stands out as the longest and only hedged choice, and both explanations use 'only'.
